Vincent E. Griego Chambers 
Basement, 1 Civic Plaza 
December 2, 2010 ● 6:00 – 8:00 p.m. 
 
Agenda 
 
Objective: 
To provide the Committee with an overview of the requirements of the federal Voting Rights Act and 
other legal principles of redistricting. 
 
Estimated Times: 
 
6:00

•

•

CITY OF ALBUQUERQUE
CITY COUNCIL
INTEROFFICE MEMORANDUM
TO:
All Councilors
FROM:
Ken Sanchez, President, City Council
Trudy Jones, Vice-President, City Council
SUBJECT:
Appointments to the 2010 Redistricting Committee 
DATE:
September 15, 2010
CC:
Laura Mason
On August 16, 2010, the City Council passed R-10-109, which creates the 
Charter required Redistricting Committee.  That Committee’s purpose is to make 
recommendations to the Council regarding redistricting the council districts based on 
2010 census data.
The Charter requires that the Redistricting Committee be composed of an equal 
number of members from each Council district, must “as nearly as practicable” provide 
fair and balanced representation of the entire City, and its membership must “reflect the 
racial, ethnic and gender makeup of the City’s population”;
On August 27, 2010 and again on September 8, 2010, the City Council held 
study sessions to discuss the proposed makeup of the Redistricting Committee.  The 
names listed below are those proposed by each Council member, and we believe that a 
Redistricting Committee comprised of these members represents, as nearly as 
practicable, the geographic, ethnic and gender makeup of the City of Albuquerque.
  
As such, we respectfully request your approval of the appointment of the 
following individuals to the city’s 2010 Redistricting Committee:

Page 3 of 4 
 
Vice-Chair Rael asked about keeping Councilors informed of the work of the Committee so they can in turn let their 
constituencies know the timeline and the reason behind the timeline.  Mr. Zaman responded that staff will be working 
with the Councilors to keep them apprised of the Committee’s work, and added that the expectation is for each 
Committee member to work with the Councilor that appointed them and it will then be up to the Councilors how and in 
what manner they want to rollout that information to their constituents.   He added that the resolution creating the 
Committee has the Committee’s preliminary recommendations going to the Council on March 1, so beginning March 1 
there will be some concepts available for the public to look at and for Councilors to take to their constituents. 
 
Vice-Chair Rael requested a timeline be provided that includes the Committee’s process deadlines as well as the 
municipal election deadlines. 
 
Mr. Gurule stressed the importance of transparency and getting the neighborhoods involved early on in the process. 
 
Vice-Chair Rael asked where else will the timeline be available for viewing by citizens.  Mr. Zaman stated the timeline 
could be placed in the Neighborhood Newsletter as well as in Ms. Bailey’s office.  Ms. Bailey stated the information will 
also be available on the City Clerk’s web site.

Mr. Sharp reviewed the estimates of current overall City population and demographics based on 2009 American 
Community Survey data.  The information provided included growth patterns exhibited from 1991-2000 and the 
similarity to the growth patterns observed from 2001-2010. 
 
Mr. Sharp’s presentation is attached to these Summary Minutes. 
 
2010 Population Estimates

Ms. Isaac inquired about what the process would be if the Committee waited an electoral cycle and the schedule changed 
and what are the legal requirements.  Mr. Zaman stated that there may be a difference of opinion about the underlying 
legal language, but the Charter says that following the receipt of census data the City must form a Redistricting 
Committee and redistrict.  He will discuss these issues with both Mr. Stelzner as well as the City Legal Department.  He 
stated that if the analysis shows that perhaps it is better to put this off to a later date, the resolution can be rescinded or 
modified to reflect that, but he did not want to speculate what Legal Counsel would say at this point. 
 
Ms. Isaac asked when the ACS data would be available.  Mr. Sharp responded it would be available in December. 
 
Ms. Isaac asked about postal service data and the volatility that exists with regard to vacant homes.  Mr. Sharp stated he 
will take the new building permits and send them through the postal service database, which will then flag those 
addresses that are not deliverable or are vacant.  He stated that should give him a good idea where the foreclosures are, 
and where building permits were issued, but nothing has been built yet and he will exclude those.

text_excerpts.2:
11.4.10 Summary Minutes 
Page 2 of 3 
In reviewing the process timeline, Mr. Zaman stated the Committee will not have the 2010 census data at the time of   
making its recommendations, but Mr. Sharp will provide preliminary data to work from.  When the final data is released 
by the Census, the Committee can modify their preliminary plans.  Once the Committee receives the final census data, 
the resolution gives the Committee fifteen days to take the final data and filter it back through the preliminary plans and 
come up with final recommendations to the Council. 
 
Mr. Zaman noted that all meetings of the Committee are public meetings and any documents distributed at the meetings 
are subject to the Inspection of Public Records Act.  He added that the resolution states that meetings will generally be 
conducted in accordance with the Council Rules of Procedure. 
 
Mr. Zaman pointed out that the resolution requires a majority vote for its final recommendation, but he added that the 
resolution also allows for a minority report. 
 
Mr. Gurule requested information from the City Charter regarding the 2000 population data by Council district. 
 
A copy of Mr. Zaman’s presentation is attached to these minutes. 
 
Overview of the Process 
Mr. Sharp reviewed the process and guidelines for collecting, presenting and managing data, and the milestone dates.  Mr. 
Sharp discussed the census data that will be used for the preliminary plans.  He stated that a database will be built using 
the estimated population data and preliminary plans will be developed based on that data and from input received by the 
Committee.

11.4.10 Summary Minutes 
Page 3 of 3 
Mr. Martinez noted the need for population data in order to accomplish the work of the Committee.  Mr. Sharp 
responded that he will have his estimated population redistricting database put together by the end of November., which 
will be a table at precinct level with all the demographics that the Committee will use to redistrict. 
 
Mr. Karpoff raised several questions for discussion with regard to procedural operations and guidelines for the 
Committee to follow, including public involvement, media relations and gathering of information. 
 
Ms. Lopez suggested that in addition to the Committee’s regular meetings, there should be one meeting held in each 
Council District to involve and engage the public and receive their input.  Mr. Barnett pointed out the compressed 
timeline and pointed out that the frequency of meetings and time commitment being discussed would be considerable. 
Mr. Johnson suggested consolidating a few of the community meetings, possibly combining 3 districts into one meeting. 
 
Mr. Martinez stated that communication is very important when involving the public.  He feels that Mr. Sharp should be 
the central repository of information. 
 
Ms. Arnold-Jones suggested the meetings be held in the Chambers and include a public comment period.  Ms. Mason 
pointed out that the City Council shares the usage of the Chambers with other entities, but staff would check with the 
Chambers scheduler in the morning. 
 
Election of a Chair and Vice-Chair 
Mr. Karpoff called for nominations for Chair.  Mr. Stratton nominated Ms. Arnold-Jones.  Ms. Lopez nominated 
Roberta M. Rael.  Mr. Gurule moved that nominations cease and the Committee go to a vote, Mr. Stratton seconded.  
The motion to cease nominations passed unanimously.  Ms. Ortega called the roll in order of Council District.  Ms. 
Arnold-Jones was elected to serve as Chair on a 5-4 vote as follows: 
 
Ms. Arnold Jones

saved_evidence.title: Redistricting Information: One Person One Vote, Minority Voting Rights, and Traditional Districting Principles (December 2, 2010)
saved_evidence.description: The committee's legal briefing sets out the constitutional and Voting Rights Act constraints on Albuquerque redistricting: the five per cent deviation rule, the three-part Section 2 vote dilution test, and the judicially recognised traditional districting principles.
saved_evidence.evidence: Image-only PDF with no text layer; page 1 was rendered and read. It states the plus or minus five per cent deviation rule, ten per cent total; names Hispanics, African Americans and Native Americans as the ethnic and language minority groups whose voting power must not be diluted; sets out the three-part Section 2 test; and flags cracking and packing as suspect practices.
saved_evidence.why_retained: The clearest statement in the inventory of the legal rules that constrain how Albuquerque may draw its council districts, in three pages. It is the kind of record that stays useful across every future redistricting cycle.

saved_evidence.description: The enacted City resolution creates the 2010 Redistricting Committee required by the City Charter, sets its charge to recommend council district boundaries from federal census data, and repeals the 2001 enactment that established the previous committee.
saved_evidence.evidence: Image-only PDF with no text layer; page 1 was rendered and read. Council Bill No. R-10-109, handwritten Enactment No. R-2010-103, Nineteenth Council, sponsored by Ken Sanchez and Trudy Jones, repealing Enactment R-2001-080 (R-01-256). The recitals set the Charter's composition requirements, the October 2011 municipal election, and the March 15, 2011 start of the candidate exploratory period.
saved_evidence.why_retained: Enacted law and the constitutive document of the whole directory: every other record here exists because this resolution created the committee. It is the fourth enacted instrument found anywhere in the Council library during this run, and the only one that carries its own date of passage in a companion memorandum also retained here.
saved_evidence.date_basis: The resolution sheet itself carries no passage date. The retained interoffice memorandum src-692f5564d80d10f0 states "On August 16, 2010, the City Council passed R-10-109", which is where the date comes from.
